Background/history
In Charmcaster's debut appearance, Tough Luck, she busted Hex out of prison and assisted him in trying to steal the Lost Keystone of Bezel which can re-create the other five charms to greatly strengthen and increase Hex's abilities. She managed to trick Gwen by putting on an act about Hex forcing her to help him, only to swipe the Keystone while hugging Gwen. She then gave Hex the Keystone. In the end, it was revealed that Hex needed the Keystone to recreate the five Charms of Bezel, and that she was planning to take their power for herself, but failed, as did Hex. To compensate for her insecurities, Charmcaster acts very arrogantly and ego-driven, striving to prove her superiority over others, Gwen above all, whose magical talents and power she is highly jealous of. She also holds resentment towards Gwen for stealing her spellbook.
Despite her faults, Charmcaster can be friendly and sociable when she feels like it. This was especially seen when she teamed up with Ben's team in Legerdomain and  Anur Transyl. She also showed that she has some morals when she saved a kid from being hit by a truck while in disguised as Caroline.[1] In the former instance, she had also relaxed and had more of a sense of humor than before, only dropping it when under the influence of the Alpha Rune's power. She has also become more childish than before, with both the cheerful innocence and the petty cruelty that comes along with it.

Powers/Ability
Like her uncle, Charmcaster depends on magic to fight. Charmcaster is highly skilled in various magical and mystical spells, although it is clear that because of her inexperience, she is not as strong and powerful as her uncle.

Similar to Gwen, Charmcaster can control the mana around her but she does so using spells and incantations. She uses her power to conjure and control a small army of Rock Monsters. She can also levitate, perform telekinesis, teleport, open portals either for viewing or transport, manipulate the elements, and transform herself into a dragon. Charmcaster can alter her appearance, such as when she assumed the form of Caroline. When Charmcaster kissed Kevin, she induced him into some sort of hypnotic trance where she apparently had full control and was able to influence his subconscious mind. This indicates that she is capable of mind control.

Equipment
Charmcaster has a magic bag from which she can draw all manner of magical mystical items, such as magical explosives in shades of glowing purple, throwing purple glowing blades, or even a variety of clay animals which she can magically enlarge and animate to do her bidding.

Although small, the bag seems to have something of a pocket dimension inside-basically a magic satchel-allowing Charmcaster to store a wide variety things within it that logically should not fit. At one point, it produces Hex's own magic staff, an item that is at least four feet tall. The bag also appears to have some degree of sentience, as it found its way back to Charmcaster under its own power.

Charmcaster possessed a miniature dark purple and gold-striped spellbook hidden in her coat until 10-year-old Gwen took it as a keepsake.

Charmcaster appearance is Charmcaster's appearance is a captivating amalgamation of style and mystique, as she dons a magenta coat adorned with elegant purple accents at its ends, exuding an air of enchantment. Beneath this striking outerwear, she elegantly sports long purple heeled boots, accented by sleek black straps, epitomizing her penchant for alluring fashion choices. A unique touch to her ensemble is her trusty magical bag, securely fastened around her waist, undoubtedly concealing a plethora of enchanting secrets. Charmcaster's long silver hair is masterfully arranged into a low ponytail, imparting an air of sophistication to her overall look. Her ethereal, light purple and pinkish eyes exude an otherworldly allure, further complemented by her carefully chosen shade of purple lipstick. Adding a touch of elegance, she adorns her ears with not one, but two earrings each, an intricate detail that accentuates her mysterious charm. The evolution of Charmcaster's appearance seamlessly merges elements from her previous "Alien Force/Ultimate Alien" incarnation with a fresh and captivating twist. Her once stark white hair now boasts enchanting purple highlights, offering a captivating contrast to her overall aesthetic. Embracing a nod to her "Original Series" look, she retains her signature ponytail, which embodies a timeless quality in her portrayal. Charmcaster's captivating eye makeup, reminiscent of the gothic "Eye of Horus" styling, adds an extra layer of enchantment to her gaze, creating an aura of enigmatic allure. Completing her ensemble, she once again opts for heeled dark-purple boots, a choice that not only accentuates her stature but also accentuates her taste for all things elegant. One remarkable facet of Charmcaster's evolution is her newfound ability to seamlessly merge with her enigmatic "Rock Monsters," a transformation that grants her a secondary armored form. In this formidable state, she retains the stone texture and hues of her creations, adding a layer of formidable mystique to her already captivating appearance. It's undeniable that Charmcaster's striking visage and undeniable allure make her a figure of remarkable attraction within the realms of her mystical adventures.


Charmcaster's personality unfolds as a multi-faceted tapestry, shaped by a tumultuous upbringing marked by the absence of paternal guidance. With no fatherly figure to steer her path, her sole mentor took the form of her enigmatic uncle, Hex. This, however, catalyzed her transformation into a complex individual bearing a delinquent attitude and an insatiable hunger for power, a characteristic that became ingrained in her essence. Her journey through life was marred by a stint in Juvenile Hall, a harrowing chapter where she endured relentless bullying, further exacerbating her already challenging path to maturity. The absence of a nurturing family environment and the trials she faced rendered her journey even more arduous. Notably, Charmcaster's character harbors a deep yearning for her absent father, a longing that led her to commit the unthinkable act of sacrificing an astonishing 600,000 souls, even including those of formidable figures like Ben, Gwen, and Kevin, in a desperate bid to resurrect him. This emotional void and her desperate quest to fill it serv e as a haunting undercurrent to her personality. To compensate for her inner insecurities and longing, Charmcaster frequently adopts an outward persona of arrogance and an unwavering ego-driven demeanor. Her relentless pursuit of power and superiority over others, particularly Gwen, reflects her profound jealousy of Gwen's innate magical talents and prowess. Moreover, her resentment towards Gwen for appropriating her spellbook only intensifies this rivalry. Beneath the layers of her imperfections, Charmcaster reveals glimpses of a more sociable and amicable nature, which surfaces on occasions when it aligns with her interests or objectives. Her capacity for friendship and collaboration became evident when she teamed up with Ben's group during their escapades in Legerdomain and Anur Transyl, showcasing a more lighthearted and humorous side to her character, temporarily shedding her usual stoicism. However, the influence of external forces, such as the power of the Alpha Rune, can induce marked shifts in her demeanor, reverting her to a more authoritarian and less affable disposition. This transformation manifests as an intriguing blend of cheerful innocence and occasional petty cruelty, reflecting her ongoing internal struggle to reconcile her myriad emotions and experiences. In summary, Charmcaster's character is a compelling study in contrasts, influenced by a tumultuous past, insecurities, and a persistent quest for power. Her multifaceted personality, oscillating between arrogance and sociability, jealousy and camaraderie, exemplifies the depths of her character, making her a captivating figure within the intricate narratives of her mystical adventures.

Charmcaster was born on Zoraster, a location in Legerdomain, under the name Hope. Her father, Spellbinder, was at war with Addwaitya at the time, and helped her and his brother Hex escape safely to Earth, but failed in battle and was murdered by Addwaitya. Growing up, Charmcaster had always dreamed of becoming a great sorceress. In Charmcaster's debut appearance, Tough Luck, she busted Hex out of prison and assisted him in trying to steal the Lost Keystone of Bezel which can re-create the other five charms to greatly strengthen and increase Hex's abilities. She managed to trick Gwen by putting on an act about Hex forcing her to help him, only to swipe the Keystone while hugging Gwen. She then gave Hex the Keystone. In the end, it was revealed that Hex needed the Keystone to recreate the five Charms of Bezel, and that she was planning to take their power for herself, but failed, as did Hex. Charmcaster returned in A Change of Face. She attempted a body swap spell with Ben as Stinkfly in Salem, Massachusetts. She was hoping to take control of the Omnitrix and combine its powers with her magic in order to become invincible. Her efforts failed, however, as her attempts only ended in swapping with Gwen. On her second try, she was returned to her normal body while Ben and Gwen were swapped, and the third time resulted in returning Ben and Gwen to their normal bodies. She was arrested at the end of the episode, and her bag was tossed into the harbor. She was last seen in juvie, where she was about to be beaten up by Pinky and Missy, whom Gwen angered during her stay in Charmcaster's body. Gwen obtained her spellbook, and kept it as a souvenir, eventually learning to use it. Charmcaster somehow escaped and made a cameo appearance at the end of Don't Drink the Water, where she was seen taunting her uncle Hex (who had been reduced in age to an infant by the waters of the Fountain of Youth) and saying that she would be giving the orders now. Charmcaster's final appearance in the Original Series was in Ben 10 vs. the Negative 10 as part of the Negative 10. Unlike her partners, however, Charmcaster was only focused on defeating Gwen (as opposed to Ben like everyone else was). She was also shown to have a small rivalry with fellow Negative 10 member Rojo. Eventually, she and the rest of her team were beaten and arrested. Charmcaster returned in In Charm's Way, where she sent one of her Rock Monsters to attack Ben, Gwen, and Kevin while they were spending the day at the beach. The Rock Monsters appeared to be immune to Gwen's mana attacks and proceeded to oust Kevin. Just as Ben was about to take down the Rock Monster, a magical portal opened up and sucked it away. It was later shown that Charmcaster was hiding in a nearby cave watching the events unfold. After voicing her deep hatred for Gwen and her plan to take something precious from her, since Gwen stole her spellbook, Charmcaster used a spell that transformed her into a blonde teenage girl named Caroline as part of her plan to charm and hypnotize Kevin. Charmcaster set her plan into motion after saving a child from being killed by a truck. Afterwards, she and Kevin journeyed to the beach where she revealed a partially false life story while removing the ID mask that concealed Kevin's mutant form, clearly growing jealous of Gwen when Kevin mentioned "You think you can do magic? She's made of magic". She then kissed him, putting him under her hypnotic influence through a spell, and then ordered him to bring Gwen to the planetarium before midnight where she could drain Gwen's magical and Anodite powers. To fortify or deepen her hypnotic control over Kevin, she also granted him a magic amulet. Kevin was broken free from Charmcaster's influence spell after the amulet was broken by Ben. After the trio arrived at the Planetarium at Gwen's request, Charmcaster sent her Rock Monsters to deal with Ben and Kevin while she dealt with Gwen herself. Upon meeting, Charmcaster gloated sarcastically at Gwen's hairdo then engaged her in a short magical duel, in which Gwen was led to stand in the middle of a circle of runes that were placed directly under the sky panel. After luring Gwen into the trap, Charmcaster opened the runes and the sky panel which exposed Gwen to the full blaze of the moonlight and brought her to her knees. This helped Charmcaster in fully subduing Gwen. She then drained Gwen of all her magic and transferred it to herself. Confident that she had won, Charmcaster retreated with her two surviving rock minions while Ben and Kevin went to Gwen's aid instead of pursuing her. After a short argument with Gwen, Kevin tricked Charmcaster into meeting him on top of a tall building where he lured her with a lie about his loyalty to Ben and that Gwen still had power left, angering Charmcaster even further. The duo later showed up at Mr Smoothy, where Ben and Gwen were drinking smoothies. After scanning Gwen, Charmcaster realized that Gwen had no power left and that Kevin managed to trick her. She used a spell to bring a Mr. Smoothy sign to life as well as controlled a parked van to kill Kevin and Ben, while her Rock Monsters attempted to annihilate Gwen, who mocked Charmcaster and proceeded to challenge her to a one-on-one fistfight, which Charmcaster nonchalantly turned down, opting to kill Gwen with a bolt of mana. However, Gwen turned the tables on Charmcaster by reciting one of her spells and reabsorbed her stolen Anodite powers from Charmcaster, much to Charmcaster's horror. Powerless, Charmcaster got help from her Rock Monsters to make one last stand against Gwen. Charmcaster was finally defeated after Gwen summoned a dimensional vortex which sucked her and her Rock Monsters away. Charmcaster appeared in Time Heals with her uncle Hex. In this episode, Hex was awakened by a disturbance in their home late at night, only for Charmcaster to convince him to return to bed. The disturbance was actually Gwen, who had snuck in to steal one of their books that had a spell that would allow for her to travel back in time in order to stop Kevin's mutation. Charmcaster returned in Hit 'Em Where They Live, where she assisted Zombozo and Vulkanus in a plot to kidnap Ben's mother. She was defeated by Kevin, who almost caused a rollercoaster to crash on her (Charmcaster escaped before getting hit); Kevin made sure she was not killed as he had promised Gwen he would not finish off his opponent. In Where the Magic Happens, Charmcaster was brought back to her home, Yawatacsip ("Legerdomain" as the natives refer to it) to bring help to Gwen and the team. In this episode, much was revealed about Charmcaster's past and her feelings toward Gwen. It was shown that Charmcaster had always dreamed of becoming a great sorceress, saying that she had studied magic her whole life but found it extremely unbelievable that Gwen could just come out of nowhere, steal her spellbook and become so strong and powerful and suddenly "out-magic" her. It is also revealed that when she was a child, her father Spellbinder and her people were at war with Addwaitya, the greatest magical, mystic being that had ever lived. Her father helped her and Hex escape safely to Earth, but failed in battle and was murdered by Addwaitya. Charmcaster's villainous actions were all to gain more and more power so that she could return to Legerdomain and defeat Addwaitya. Charmcaster moved past her feelings of resentment toward Gwen and actually developed a friendship with her, chiefly due to learning that the two of them were actually stronger and more powerful as a team than individually; her knowledge of magic coupled with Gwen's Anodite powers. She even ended up putting her life on the line, buying time for the trio to escape, leaving herself behind in Legerdomain with the hopes of defeating Addwaitya at last. In Enemy of My Frenemy, Charmcaster had become corrupted with power during her time fighting for Legerdomain and relapsed into her evil ways when the denizens she had fought to free from Addwaitya turned on her and fought a massive civil war to decide who would become the new ruler; a war which Charmcaster won. Building a device that drains the souls out of living things, she enacted a plan to drain the life force of her world in order to perform a ritual that would bring her father Spellbinder back to life. Ben, Gwen, and Kevin attempted to stop her, but their souls were sucked out as well. When Spellbinder was resurrected, he revealed that Charmcaster's real name is Hope. Horrified at the lengths his daughter had gone to in order to bring him back, he said he couldn't stay at the cost of so many souls. Telling his daughter that he loved her, he faded away, making the ritual null and void and returning all souls back to where they belonged. Charmcaster broke down crying, not knowing what to do with her life now. Out of pity, Ben, Gwen, and Kevin agreed not to arrest the heartbroken Charmcaster and departed from Legerdomain. In Couples Retreat, Charmcaster fell in love with Darkstar when he attempted to get into Legerdomain. She supplied him with a lot of mana when they kissed multiple times and allowed him to go back to Earth to take revenge upon "his enemies", not knowing this to be Ben, Gwen and Kevin. She also revealed her true name, Hope, to him. When Ben, Gwen, and Kevin arrived at her castle, she fought Gwen while Ben and Kevin took on Darkstar. She became enraged when she learned Darkstar and Gwen once dated. Gwen, concerned about Charmcaster, tried to convince her that Darkstar was merely using her, but Hope seemed hopelessly deluded. However, just as Darkstar offered her the chance to team up with him and conquer Earth, she realized that Gwen might be right and asked Darkstar why he never called her by her real name, and if he even remembers it. After Darkstar didn't, Hope became so enraged that her screams destroyed her castle, then drained Darkstar's powers and banished him from Legerdomain, leaving him at the mercy of Ben, Gwen, and Kevin waiting to beat him up. Charmcaster was last seen at the ruins of her castle, sadly gazing down upon Darkstar's helmet. By the time of the Omniverse series, she is gradually becoming corrupted again, this time partially due to an outside influence. Charmcaster made an appearance in Mystery, Incorporeal where she appeared driving the police car carrying Darkstar disguised as a police officer. When asked if she had forgiven him, she responded by turning him into a totem. In Charmed, I'm Sure, Charmcaster appeared on Anur Transyl to take back the Alpha Rune, which had been stolen by Zs'Skayr. She teamed up with Ben, Rook Blonko, and Hobble (who had a crush on her) to get it back. When they reached Zs'Skayr, he gave the Rune back willingly since he had already drained it of much of its power. Charmcaster put the Rune on and went mad with its power, summoning Rock Monsters that she turned into battle armor for herself. She suddenly turned on Ben and attacked him, but she was defeated when Hobble threw the magical artifacts in Rook's arsenal at her, which destroyed her armor. Rook then used a teleportation spell from Gwen's spellbook to teleport her back to Legerdomain. In Legerdomain, it was revealed that Charmcaster betrayed Ben under the advice of Addwaitya, who had been turned into a stone totem that was kept in her bag along with Darkstar, both of whom she had been speaking with all episode (leading others to believe her to be crazy since only she could hear them). Addwaitya assured her that she will be successful next time, to which Charmcaster threatened him to remember that she controlled him now, not the other way around. When she asked why she shouldn't just smash both of them, Darkstar whispered a plan into her ear that she evidently liked. In Charm School, Charmcaster attended Friedkin University at Hex's word, hoping that the two of them could be closer. However, Charmcaster only came to Friedkin University to obtain a powerful artifact known as the Staff of Ages. Charmcaster's first attempt that getting the Staff of Ages was a failure due to Hex being powerful in his library. However, Charmcaster managed to turn Hex into a totem after impersonating Professor Xagliv. Charmcaster obtained the Staff of Ages from a book in Hex's library but it was soon taken away by Gwen. Charmcaster managed to take back the Staff of Ages and completely overwhelm Gwen due to Charmcaster possessing Hex while in his library. Charmcaster continued to fight Gwen until Ben as Ghostfreak joined in the fight along with Kevin, Rook, and Zed. Charmcaster summoned some rock bats and had them go after Kevin, Rook, and Zed while Charmcaster went after Gwen and Ghostfreak. Charmcaster easily defeated Ghostfreak and sent him flying into the library. However, Charmcaster was then outmatched by Gwen who took back the Hex totem and was more powerful in the library. Charmcaster lost the Staff of Ages and was sent back to Legerdomain. In Third Time's a Charm, Charmcaster lured Gwen to Legerdomain and turned her into a totem. When she returned to the library at Friedkin University, she learned of Bezel's presence there and tried to take his power. She succeeded when she turned him into a totem, and then attempted to destroy Ben, Rook and Kevin, even transforming into a dragon. Ben and Gwen tricked her into getting turned into a totem and sealed into her own bag, which she declared a temporary setback and vowed revenge. Gwen kept Charmcaster, still inside the bag, in her headquarters and was hopeful that under these circumstances the two of them can finally be friends. Charmcaster appeared, no longer a totem, as one of the many female contestants vying to marry Ben in The Most Dangerous Game Show. She lost in the third round when she flew across a lava pit only to crashland on a floating rock when a lava bubble burst dangerously close to her. She was then transported to the Null Void along with the other losers, until Ben arrived to set them free. Charmcaster, along with the other girls, helped to save Ben from the Way Bads before returning to Earth to help him face Charles Zenith. Following The Most Dangerous Game Show, Charmcaster probably got magically zapped back into her bag.

She wore her long silver hair laid out that extended to her thighs, orchid eyes, and very dark purple lipstick. entries.content:
The Omnitrix resembles a digital wristwatch. Its faceplate is now square rather than round and has a white, green, and black color scheme. The faceplate is black with two green stripes forming an outline for the hourglass of the Galvan tech logo. When the faceplate is slid back, the Omnitrix's core is revealed.

Features
General
Just like the original Omnitrix and the Ultimatrix, the Omnitrix mainly allows for the user to alter their DNA at will and transform into a numerous variety of alien species that are each with their own unique powers and abilities (along with their weaknesses) and in a selection of alien DNA that is in groups of 10.
The Omnitrix has a quick-change feature that allows for the user to transform between alien forms while already transformed with or without touching the Omnitrix symbol. It also allows the user to transform back into normal when they are done using their transformation, causing it not to time out and allowing the user to transform again far quicker.
The Omnitrix has a Master Control, which would most likely be activated upon the user's 18th birthday.
The Omnitrix can synchronize with another Omnitrix if activated at the same time.
The Omnitrix does not rely on the Codon Stream for transformation. Instead, the DNA is stored within itself in a computerized form.
The Omnitrix can change the user's gender to adapt to another species.
The Omnitrix has Call mode which is used to communicate with the user using the device.
The Omnitrix is waterproof

Extensions
The Omnitrix has a 2-way communication system with Plumber Badges.
The Omnitrix can also record messages, similar to voicemail.
The Omnitrix has the functionalities of a regular digital watch.
The Omnitrix has a function were the user to stay transformed for an extended period of time without timing out.
The Omnitrix has a built-in Universal Translator and could also translate other Earth languages.
The Omnitrix has a distress signal function and homing device.
The Omnitrix has a security lock system so that it can only be used by the user, as well as an alternate identification program if changes by outside forces occur to the user.
The Omnitrix has a failsafe that kicks in the event that the user's life is in jeopardy. This feature turns them into the needed alien to survive.
The Omnitrix has failsafes installed by Azmuth that prevent Galvanic Mechamorphs from tampering with the device.
The Omnitrix can add extras to lifeforms to make them safer and more usable, such as Goop's Anti-Gravity Projector and NRG's containment suit.

Allocation
The Omnitrix symbol is positioned on different places for each alien whenever the user is transformed.

Voice Command
The Omnitrix can be controlled by Voice Command.
Omnitrix User Access Voice Recognition Mode: Makes the Omnitrix recognize the user.
Command Code 1010 Tennyson Benjamin Disengage Life-Form Lock: Disengages Life-Form lock.

Modes
Active Mode
Active Mode is the Omnitrix's default mode when idle. It is where the user can select the transformation they want to become; initiate the process of transforming; and stay in said transformation. The actual usage time is 15 minutes at a time. However, different factors and actions performed by the user can severely diminish the available usage time: most commonly if the user, while transformed, changes to another form. If the user slamming the core, this affects the time limit of a transformation, as the user could stay transformed for hours.

Recharge Mode
When the Omnitrix's usage time is fully depleted (i.e. "times out"), it goes into Recharge Mode: firstly warning of the timing out; then detransforming the user and locking all functions of Active Mode while the Omnitrix recharges.

Time Out
The Omnitrix is capable of detecting when it's host is in any sort of life-threatening distress. Specifically, it can instantly recharge to protect the user from a direct physical threat.

If the user is knocked out or hurt enough, the Omnitrix will revert them to their normal form.

Collect Mode
When a new DNA sample has been unlocked, or when the Omnitrix captures new DNA not present in the catalog, Collect Mode is activated. However, if the Omnitrix is far away from the detected sample, the Omnitrix's other functions will be disabled until the alien is scanned.

The Omnitrix symbol shooting green ray
When in alien form, the Omnitrix shoots out a green ray from the dial.

When the Omnitrix scans the DNA of an alien it doesn't have, it won't always be immediately unlocked in the arsenal.

Self-Destruct
The Omnitrix has a self-destruction mode. In this mode, the Omnitrix will begin a countdown, beeping as a warning that the mode has been activated. It can be enabled if settings are changed, and can be disabled if settings are changed again.

Randomizer
The Omnitrix has a randomizer function that works in one of two ways: either the user will continuously change between different aliens every few minutes before timing out, or they will turn into one random alien for an inconsistently short period of time before changing back.

Malfunctions
If the Omnitrix does mis-transform, it is because of the user slamming on the Omnitrix's core too hard and (inadvertently) the scroll pad.
Much like the Ultimatrix, the Omnitrix is not hack proof.
Much like the original Omnitrix, the Omnitrix does not have a failsafe against magic. If the Omnitrix symbol is bitten by magic creatures, such as rock monsters, the device will send a shockwave, distransform the user and will select only one alien.
Like the original Omnitrix, on occasion any damage the user sustains was retained when said user times out.
The DNA Scanner of the Omnitrix will attempt to scan any new DNA in the vicinity. If the DNA sample is too far away, then the Omnitrix will shut down all its other functions until it scans the new sample.
The user can be prevented from transforming by the Forever Knights DNA Scanner which would scan the transformations DNA before reveting the user.
Too many transformations and reversals will wear out the Omnitrix, causing it to go into a cooldown cycle.
The Omnitrix has no mind control protection.
The Omnitrix may stop working when frozen in time by a Chronosapien.
In addition to gaining all the powers and abilities of an alien, the user gains all the weaknesses of that alien as well. One common weakness includes being vulnerable to the alien's natural predator. The user is also susceptible to certain behaviors inherent to the alien he/she is transformed into, such as Swampfire's evolution, and the Swarm Gastronomy of Upchuck.
Upon activating the Randomizer Function, the user will constantly switch transformations at the most inopportune times, thereby putting them into potentially dangerous situations.
When exposed to electromagnetic interference from beings like Phil, it can make the Omnitrix transform the user into electrical aliens even when they select a different alien.
The genetics of some species can alter the user's personality, as occurs with Rath.
If tampered with by Eon, the Omnitrix can transfer the user's mind in cross-time to a younger version.

Atomix wears the Omnitrix symbol on his green and white belt.

Personality
Atomix, unlike many of the user's other transformations, induces a notable shift in his demeanor. He adopts a highly formal and almost theatrical persona, characterized by a strong sense of justice and a penchant for grand pronouncements. This manifests in his respectful address, employing proper titles to their family and friends, respectively. Furthermore, he possesses a flair for dramatic flair, frequently naming his powerful attacks in a style reminiscent of anime heroes.

Atomix can create nuclear energy using his hands, which can do a massive amount of damage to its surroundings.

The way Atomix creates his nuclear blasts is by chanting "HAA-MEE-NA HAA-MEE-NA HAA-MEE-NA-HA!" It is not crucial for him to chant every attack, but doing so will focus an attack's power and cause substantially more damage.

Atomix is capable of flight and, as such, he can perform a flying ramming attack called the Fissile Whistle.

Atomix's hard body gives him substantial protection against physical attacks.

Atomix can glow in the dark.

Rath almost always speaks in third person and a loud voice. Sometimes, when he becomes extremely angry, he mixes up metaphors (such as "a man's food is his castle" or "you just bit off an eye that's bigger than your stomach can chew"). He is aware that they do not make sense, but still continues to use them anyway.

Rath's muscle-over-brains mindset makes him needlessly argue with everyone around him. He even shouts at inanimate objects, like a hole he made in the ground, a stolen spaceship, gravity, water, fire, the Omnitrix and Ultimatrix for their malfunctions, the laser pointers, a giant ball of yarn, and a paper bag on his head, arguments of which were ridiculous and that occasionally lead him to harm both himself and others. Rath's confrontational attitude often gets him and his teammates into trouble.

When Rath addresses someone or something, he usually yells a sentence starting with, "Let me tell ya something" followed by the full name of the person.

He closely resembles an approximately seven-foot-tall muscular human male, with four fingers on each hand and black hair with sideburns. Most of his skin is a dull, greyish yellow; however, some areas on his body have a different skin tone, which are separated by scars and what resembles sutures, as if his body parts were sewn together. He wears metal gauntlets that end in fingerless gloves; metallic boots with grills on them; and dark, shiny pants with ribs that dip in a V-shape. He has many bolts that resemble flathead screws in places all over his upper body; and he has two large tower-shaped, conductor coil-like generators located on his upper back; though these are metallic-organic growths and not actually machines.

Frankenstrike's hair is cut much shorter, though his sideburns have increased in length in a mutton chops-style. His two-toned skin returns, the second tone now being a more withered dark grey. Patches of it are located on his entire left shoulder and left pectoral; his entire right forearm; the top of his right shoulder; one spot on the middle-right of his back; and nearly completely covering his neck and face, save for some of the right side of his face. Suturing connects all the patches, as well as a circular "cut" around his cranium. Frankenstrike's bolts are now much larger and stumpier; they are a copper color, with green lines stretching across and off the tips. There are now 3 bolts on his back; 6 for each side of his neck, shoulder, and elbow; and one on his belt, where the Omnitrix used to be. His conductors have moved up more from his back and cover his trapezius muscles. They are now a deep green, with white coils and light green bulbs at the tips. His belt and gauntlets are green, with small screws appearing along their white stripe and knuckles, respectively. His pants are very dark green and his boots are copper with light green slits. Frankenstrike's teeth are now yellowed and uneven, and bear out. The Omnitrix symbol is embedded in the flesh of his right pectoral, with several deep scars protruding from where it resides.

He wears a black jumpsuit with a green chest and markings, black gloves with green fingers that possess sharp claws, and a green mask with spikes on it. His head is rather large and features green eyes, and his head spikes are part of his suit and they do not cover any part of his body. Whampire also has green flaps under his arms, which resemble the wings of a bat.

Whampire wears the Omnitrix symbol on his stomach.

Whampire's Corrupturas are crystalline entities, they are small, dark green, diamond-shaped objects with light green eyes, little horns, and black bat-like wings.

In his bat form, Whampire becomes a small black ball with wings of the same color and size. A miniature version of his face is on the front of his body.

While burning in sunlight, Whampire's clothes seem to burn off first, leaving his skin, which would be completely grey due to the sun, exposed before he himself burns.

Powers and Abilities
Quadrupedalism
Whampire's species are masters of controlling other beings. This gives him both the ability to hypnotize other beings through eye contact, and the ability to control beings by shooting Corrupturas at their foreheads. He can produce these small creatures from his mouth and can generate ones of different sizes to suit the size of his victim.

Whampire's Corrupturas are effective on other races of the Anur System.

Whampire can absorb and feed off the energy of living beings by sucking on them. He can even drain the life force of a Celestialsapien. If Whampire were to completely drain his victims of their energy, they would look similar to Darkstar's victims.

Whampire has the ability to fly and is highly agile while in flight.

Whampire has a certain level of enhanced strength, being able to hold his own against a mob of Anur Transyl citizens before eventually being overrun.

Whampire can withstand other Vladats hypnotizing him depending on his willpower.

Whampire can create a huge sonic explosion as a last-resort means of self-defense that was powerful enough to send everyone flying in every direction.

Whampire can survive in the vacuum of space.

Like all Anur System aliens, Whampire can see in the dark.

Whampire can control undead aliens and inanimate objects that are supernaturally possessed, using his Corrupturas. In the case of the latter, the object would have to contain the possessor's consciousness.

entries.name: Toepick
entries.content:
Toepick is the Omnitrix's DNA sample of an unknown species from an unknown planet.

Apperance
Body: Ogre
Equipment: Containment Helmet
Toepick is a greenish yellow-skinned, ogre-like alien with long and misshapen arms that have weed-like spikes coming out of them, pointy fingertips, and a visible belly button. He wears a simple pair of black briefs with a metal dark green waistline with white bolts on it. His eyes are glowing green and can be seen through the bars of a dark green metal cage helmet worn on his head. Inside his helmet is Toepick's terrifying face, which is supposed to resemble an eldritch horror. He also has a layer of tentacles that covers his true face.

Toepick's helmet has two horns protruding from the sides of it, and also a crest that resembles a toenail in shape. The cage's door has five bars, three of which are in the center of the door. It opens in two halves, with the lock in the very center of the door, staying on the right half. Connected to this cage is Toepick's armor, which wraps around his shoulders and goes halfway down his chest, and is connected to his briefs by chains.

Toepick's Omnitrix symbol is on the helmet's extension covering his chest, with two green metallic protrusions accompanying the symbol on both sides.

Powers and Abilities
Toepick's only known way of defeating his enemies is with his extremely scary face, which taps into the primordial fears locked in all beings' subconscious and primitive brains. Toepick's face is so hideously horrifying that almost no being in the known universe can look at it without being scared to the point of turning pale white. If someone were to take a photograph of Toepick's face, the picture would come out blurry, but it would still make people uneasy.

The sight of Toepick's face can cause adverse effects. The most common of these effects are the inducement of terror and insanity.

Toepick's face can also induce sickness and nausea.

Toepick can counteract forces that feed on fear.

Toepick has a type of layered multiphasic eyesight that makes his already mediocre vision even worse when looking at multidimensional or unknowable sights, meaning that he cannot be frightened by his own face if he were to look into anything reflective.

Toepick is able to bulge his eyes outwards.

When Toepick's helmet prepares to open, it releases a small amount of green gases as it depressurizes. It is also incredibly difficult to damage.

Toepick has a degree of enhanced strength, enough to lift a car.

Abilities

Nightmarish Sounds
Fear Inducement
Gas Generation

Pesky Dust wears a green dress-like outfit with black zigzags, the bottommost one of which is slightly asymmetrical. His hands have three fingers with white gloves on them and his feet have two toes. His eyes are green with feminine eyelines and has pink markings on his cheeks and chin.

Pesky Dust wears the Omnitrix symbol on his chest.

Powers and Abilities
Pesky Dust is capable of flight and possesses enhanced speed and agility thanks to his fairy-like wings. He can also leave behind a green trail while flying.

Pesky Dust can release a special kind of dust that makes his victims fall asleep.

Pesky Dust can enter and examine the dreams of other beings, which can be used as a form of interrogation or extracting information from a victim. However, they must be affected by Pesky Dust's sleep dust in order for him to enter their dreams.

Pesky Dust can control the dreams of multiple victims at once.

If Pesky Dust were to keep dousing a victim in his sleeping dust, they would end up sleeping forever.

Pesky Dust can manipulate a victim's dreams, causing them to have nightmares instead.
